title: Graph-dependent pooling: adaptive granularity in hierarchical graph neural networks
abstract: arXiv:2610.33623v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Graph Neural Networks are widely used to learn structural representations of relational data. Hierarchical graph pooling learns multi-level representations by progressively coarsening graphs; however, prior methods rely on predefined cluster numbers or fixed pooling ratios, limiting adaptability to individual graphs. We propose Graph-Dependent Pooling (GDPool), which dynamically determines pooling granularity for each graph. We analyze optimization conflicts among layer-wise objectives through gradient alignment, showing that independently supervised pooling levels can send conflicting gradients to shared parameters. GDPool uses self-attention to select graph-specific anchors representing structurally important nodes and constructs coarse graphs through soft node assignment. Experiments on metal-organic framework and molecular graph benchmarks show that GDPool consistently achieves the best predictive performance across all benchmarks. E

translated_title: 图依赖池化：层次图神经网络中的自适应粒度
translated_abstract: 图神经网络被广泛用于学习关系数据的结构表示。层次图池化通过逐步粗化图来学习多层次表示；然而，先前的方法依赖于预定义的聚类数量或固定的池化比例，限制了对单个图的适应性。我们提出了图依赖池化（GDPool），它能为每个图动态确定池化粒度。我们通过梯度对齐分析了各层目标之间的优化冲突，表明独立监督的池化层可能会向共享参数发送相互冲突的梯度。GDPool使用自注意力机制选择代表结构重要节点的图特定锚点，并通过软节点分配构建粗化图。在金属有机框架和分子图基准上的实验表明，GDPool在所有基准上均持续取得了最佳的预测性能。
tldr: 提出图依赖池化（GDPool），利用自注意力机制为每个图动态确定池化粒度，并通过梯度对齐分析揭示层次池化各层目标间的优化冲突，在金属有机框架和分子图基准上均取得最佳预测性能。
en_tdlr: GDPool dynamically determines pooling granularity for each graph via self-attention, reveals optimization conflicts among layer-wise pooling objectives through gradient alignment, and consistently achieves the best predictive performance on metal-organic framework and molecular graph benchmarks.
